title: Paneer Manchurian
subtitle: Restaurant-style Indo-Chinese starter — crisp fried paneer tossed in a sweet, tangy, peppery Manchurian sauce.
protein: ~12–14g protein per adult serving — from paneer

method.title: Batter and slurry
items: Heat {@oil-fry} in a kadai for deep frying
While it heats, mix {@cornflour-batter}, {@maida} and {@salt-batter} in a bowl
Add {@water-batter} just enough for a free-flowing batter — moderately thick, not too thick or too runny
In a small bowl, stir {@cornflour-slurry} into {@water:slurry} until lump-free; keep aside

method.label: Toddler — fry her paneer first (before the chili goes in the batter)
items: Dip {@paneer:toddler} in the plain batter and fry on medium until golden and crisp
Drain on kitchen paper and set aside in her bowl — she gets a spoon of sauce later

method.title: Fry the paneer
items: Stir {@chili-powder} into the remaining batter
Dip {@paneer:main|the remaining paneer cubes} in the batter and deep fry in the hot oil
Stir often and fry on medium heat until golden and crisp
Drain on kitchen paper

method.title: Make the sauce
items: Heat {@oil} in a wide pan on high; add {@hing}
Add {@ginger}; sauté 1 min, until the aroma comes out
Add {@celery}; fry 1–2 min
Add {@capsicum}; sauté another minute
Stir the slurry once, then pour it in with {@soy} and {@ketchup}
Add {@water:adjust} if it's too thick; reduce the flame to medium and add {@sugar}

method.label: Toddler — her sauce (before pepper and vinegar)
items: Spoon {=1 tbsp} of the sauce with a few soft capsicum pieces over her paneer and toss

method.title: Toss and serve
items: Taste the sauce; add {@pepper}, plus {@salt} and {@vinegar} if needed
Let the sauce turn thick, then turn off the flame
Add {@paneer:main|the fried paneer} and {@celery-leaves}
Toss so the sauce coats every piece evenly; serve hot

method.label: Tip
method.text: Garlic → extra ginger + hing; spring onion whites → celery; spring onion greens → celery leaves or coriander. Most ketchups aren't Jain — use a no-onion-no-garlic one. Air fryer instead of deep frying: coat the cubes in a thick batter, spray with oil and cook in the Ninja Crispi at 360°F for 8–10 min, shaking once. Serve with noodles or fried rice. Best in a kadai on the stove; the Ninja Crispi is the lighter option for the paneer (see above).
